findings.description: STRONGEST FINDING. SHEET-MARK-008 is silent on what happens if the settle pass cannot parse the Quote Date cell (empty/malformed) while the companion Price cell DOES parse as Numeric. The real code (adapters.rs, price_reading_from_cells, inside the `Ok(price_usd) =>` arm) does: `cells.get(QUOTE_DATE_COL).and_then(|s| s.trim().parse::<i32>().ok()).unwrap_or(0)` — silently substituting the literal value 0 (i.e. Date(0), the 1970-01-01 epoch) with no error, no distinct DegradeReason, and no signal that the quote date is actually unknown; this path is not covered by formula.rs (which only tests the formula STRING, never this read-back branch), so it is also an untested fallback. All three independent B-reconstructions (B1 UB2, B2's 'default quote_date to Date(0)... rather than erroring', B3's 'default the parsed quote date to 0... rather than erroring') pin this identical silent-default behavior — high B-side agreement that this is real, deliberate code behavior the spec text never states. Notably, all three A-side implementations (working from the EARS text alone, which never discusses this failure case) independently chose the opposite design — returning `None`/no-value on unparseable input rather than fabricating a date — which is circumstantial evidence that 'silently claim epoch-1970' is a surprising, spec-unsanctioned choice rather than an obvious one. A downstream reader of `Mark.quote_date` (staleness display, history point) could be shown a fabricated 'quoted as of 1970-01-01' instead of any indication the quote date is actually unknown.

All three B-reconstructions pin the Quote Date column at a FIXED position: index 12 (0-based, the last/13th column on Positions), matching `QUOTE_DATE_COL: usize = 12` in adapters.rs and the test's `assert_eq!(qcol, 12, ...)`. SHEET-MARK-008 says nothing about column position/layout — it only describes the formula's semantics. Purely a code/test-pinned structural constant with no spec-text basis (expected as an implementation detail, but material because a future column reorder would silently desync the settle-pass adapter's hardcoded index from the header, with no compile-time or spec-level check tying them together).

The real formula and all three B-reconstructions pin the specific GOOGLEFINANCE attribute string `"tradetime"` (`GOOGLEFINANCE("<ticker>","tradetime")`) — the spec only says 'GOOGLEFINANCE's trade date,' naming no attribute. This is the exact site where the A-direction assumption split: 2 of 3 A-runs (A1, A3) guessed a non-existent attribute `"tradedate"` instead, while only A2 happened to land on the real `"tradetime"`. Per the classification rubric this A-side split is an assumption artifact (no basis in spec text), not a standalone A-finding — but it sharpens the B-side finding: the attribute name is a load-bearing constant the spec leaves completely open, and B unanimously (and correctly) recovered the real one.

The real formula wraps the ENTIRE expression in one outer `IFERROR(...,"")` with no separate `ISNUMBER` guard — pinned verbatim by all 3 B-reconstructions and the test's `assert!(text.contains("IFERROR"))` (with no corresponding ISNUMBER assertion). Two of three A-implementations (A1, A2) instead added a defensive `ISNUMBER(GOOGLEFINANCE(...))` check in addition to IFERROR, reasoning that GOOGLEFINANCE might emit a non-error 'Loading...' placeholder IFERROR alone wouldn't catch. The spec's parenthetical 'empty while loading/errored' doesn't distinguish these two error-handling strategies, so the shipped code embeds a narrower assumption (bare IFERROR suffices) than a majority of fresh spec-only implementations independently judged necessary — worth flagging as a place the code is doing less defensive work than the spec's phrasing invites.

The settle-pass read-back parses the Quote Date cell as a signed 32-bit integer (`.parse::<i32>()`), pinned identically by all three B-reconstructions (B2/B3 explicitly say 'signed 32-bit integer'). SHEET-MARK-008 only says 'integer count of days since 1970-01-01' with no bit width. All three A-implementations independently chose `i64` instead (reasoning about headroom / negative pre-1970 dates). Immaterial in practice (i32 covers millions of years) but is a concretely different pinned type on the B side versus the uniform A-side choice, with the spec silent on which is correct.

notes:
Read all three real files in full (sheets-view/src/lib.rs, runtime/src/adapters.rs, sheets-view/tests/formula.rs) before classifying.

Direction A (medium agreement): all three converge on the macro-shape SHEET-MARK-008 actually asks for — TEXT-formatted digit string, INT/truncate then subtract DATE(1970,1,1), IFERROR→empty on load/error, parser trims+parses to an integer, treating unparseable as a non-value rather than erroring outright. They diverge on: the invented GOOGLEFINANCE attribute name (2x "tradedate" vs 1x "tradetime", the real one), the error-guard mechanism (ISNUMBER-augmented IFERROR in A1/A2 vs. gating on a separate price cell in A3, a real difference in function signature/arity — A3 takes two cell refs, A1/A2 take one), and integer width (all chose i64 vs. real i32). None of these divergences trace to explicit spec text describing that specific sub-decision, so per the rubric they are assumption artifacts, not A-side findings — Direction A surfaces no valid spec-states/code-lacks gap here.

Direction B (high agreement): all three reconstructions independently produced near-verbatim-identical pins: the literal formula string, column index 12, the "tradetime" attribute, the i32 parse, and — most importantly — the silent `unwrap_or(0)` default-to-Date(0) on an unparseable Quote Date cell when Price is otherwise Numeric. That last item is genuine code-side surplus behavior (a real, load-bearing, currently-untested failure-mode decision) that SHEET-MARK-008's text never addresses, which drove the overall classification to B-ONLY-DRIFT rather than BD-COHERENT. I considered classifying as BD-DRIFT given the A-side's uniform (but spec-unsupported) choice of the opposite behavior, but per the stated rubric that A-side convergence doesn't qualify as a standalone A-finding since it doesn't trace to explicit spec text — so the material drift lives on the B side only.
